# Data from the Treasury Bulletin for 1940
# Individual and Corporation income tax collections (in thousands of dollars)

# January 1940
jan_individual = 20561
jan_corporation = 25128

# February 1940
feb_individual = 43443
feb_corporation = 27503

# March 1940
mar_individual = 356076
mar_corporation = 298548

# Calculate ratios (individual / corporation)
jan_ratio = jan_individual / jan_corporation
feb_ratio = feb_individual / feb_corporation
mar_ratio = mar_individual / mar_corporation

print(f"January 1940: Individual={jan_individual}, Corporation={jan_corporation}, Ratio={jan_ratio:.6f}")
print(f"February 1940: Individual={feb_individual}, Corporation={feb_corporation}, Ratio={feb_ratio:.6f}")
print(f"March 1940: Individual={mar_individual}, Corporation={mar_corporation}, Ratio={mar_ratio:.6f}")

# Now fit linear regression: months (1, 2, 3) vs ratios
# Using manual calculation for linear regression

x = [1, 2, 3]  # months
y = [jan_ratio, feb_ratio, mar_ratio]  # ratios

n = len(x)
sum_x = sum(x)
sum_y = sum(y)
sum_xy = sum([x[i]*y[i] for i in range(n)])
sum_x2 = sum([xi**2 for i, xi in enumerate(x)])

# Calculate slope (b) and intercept (a)
slope = (n * sum_xy - sum_x * sum_y) / (n * sum_x2 - sum_x**2)
intercept = (sum_y - slope * sum_x) / n

print(f"\nLinear regression: y = {slope:.6f} * x + {intercept:.6f}")
print(f"Slope coefficient: {slope:.6f}")
print(f"Slope rounded to thousandths: {round(slope, 3)}")

# Verify
print(f"\nVerification:")
for i, month in enumerate(x):
    predicted = slope * month + intercept
    print(f"  Month {month}: actual={y[i]:.6f}, predicted={predicted:.6f}")
